categories.main_business_segments: Chuo Warehouse Co., Ltd. operates three main business segments: Domestic Logistics (including warehousing and transportation), International Cargo (including packing and customs clearance), and Real Estate Leasing (leasing of logistics and non-logistics properties). The Domestic Logistics segment is the core, providing storage, distribution processing, and transportation services, while the International Cargo segment focuses on export packing and customs brokerage. The Real Estate Leasing segment manages rental properties, mainly logistics facilities and some non-logistics assets.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages advanced warehousing management, temperature and humidity-controlled storage, bonded warehouse operations, and specialized facilities for hazardous materials and trunk rooms. It also provides value-added logistics services such as distribution processing (inspection, packaging, labeling), and utilizes ISO-certified quality and information security management systems. In international cargo, it specializes in export packing for precision machinery and offers integrated logistics solutions including customs clearance and multimodal transport.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Chuo Warehouse serves a diverse range of industries, with a historical focus on textiles, chemicals, and industrial goods, but also handles food, precision machinery, and recycled materials. Its customer base includes manufacturers, trading companies, and import/export businesses, with no single customer accounting for more than 10% of revenue. The company is also expanding into circular economy logistics, such as recycled PET resin handling.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company’s operations are concentrated in Japan, with major logistics centers and offices in Kyoto, Osaka, Nagoya, Tokyo, Shiga, Hokuriku, Okayama, and other regions. Internationally, it has a presence in Shanghai, China, through a related company, but over 90% of revenue and assets are Japan-based.
categories.supply_chain_position: Chuo Warehouse operates primarily as a midstream logistics provider, acting as an intermediary between manufacturers/traders and end-users by offering storage, distribution, and transportation services. It also provides upstream support in export packing and customs clearance, and downstream services through value-added logistics and real estate leasing.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include expanding into growth areas such as recycled materials logistics, strengthening value-added logistics (e.g., machinery installation), and enhancing digital transformation (DX) in collaboration with clients. The company is investing in IT system upgrades, sustainability (CO2 reduction, LED lighting, solar power), and human capital (diversity, training, work-life balance). M&A is also considered for business expansion. There is no mention of traditional R&D activities.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated from service fees for warehousing, transportation, packing, customs clearance, and property leasing. The company recognizes revenue upon completion of services or over the service period, depending on contract terms. Product sales (e.g., packing materials) are a minor component.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Chuo Warehouse operates in a highly competitive logistics sector with many similar-sized and larger players, including other warehouse and transport companies. It maintains a stable position through diversified services, high service quality, and strong regional networks, but faces ongoing price and service competition. Major competitors include other listed Japanese logistics and warehouse firms.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending March 2025, consolidated revenue was approximately 27.8 billion yen, with operating profit of 2.19 billion yen and net profit attributable to shareholders of 1.59 billion yen. The company has around 700 employees (including part-time), a strong equity ratio (77.7%), and stable but moderate growth (5% revenue increase year-on-year). Capital investment is ongoing, with a new logistics center planned in Aichi Prefecture.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Chuo Warehouse differentiates itself through comprehensive, high-quality logistics solutions tailored to diverse customer needs, including specialized storage (temperature/humidity control, hazardous goods), value-added processing, and integrated international logistics. Its strengths include long-standing expertise, robust regional networks, and a commitment to sustainability and digital transformation. The company emphasizes reliability, flexibility, and the ability to handle complex, multi-industry logistics requirements.
